faq.answer: No. Duty, money, safety, discrimination, or limited support may require endurance. Compare meaning attention under matched strain and safer conditions.
faq.question: Does enduring hardship establish self-preservation Type Four?

faq.answer: A person cannot be interpreted as choosing restraint when asking for help carries punishment, cost, or no realistic response. Power and resources belong in the comparison.
faq.question: Why record whether help is genuinely available?

faq.answer: Restraint that vanishes in safety, effort with no recurring personal meaning, or easy acceptance of support without identity concern should weaken it.
faq.question: What weakens the contained-meaning hypothesis?

sections.body_md: The traditional description proposes that Type Four meaning may be carried through effort and restraint rather than overt expression. It is a prompt, not an explanation of why someone endures.
sections.title: Treat contained effort as a traditional hypothesis

sections.body_md: Compare similar difficult tasks in a safe voluntary setting and a setting where disclosure has costs. Record effort, meaning, help-seeking, available choice, and what changes when strain eases.
sections.title: Match strain while changing disclosure safety

sections.body_md: The label organizes observations about practical strain, continuity, and expression. It is not evidence about bodily mechanisms, a biological category, or fixed tolerance.
sections.title: Keep self-preservation language non-mechanistic

sections.body_md: Personally significant struggle may be kept private or converted into dependable action. That variation must be tested against necessity, learned restraint, and cultural expectations.
sections.title: Allow restrained expression to differ from the stereotype

sections.body_md: Caregiving, poverty, discrimination, unsafe workplaces, migration, and lack of support can make endurance necessary. Record whether refusal and help are genuinely available.
sections.title: Test duty, money, and safety

sections.body_md: The hypothesis weakens when contained expression disappears as soon as safety improves, effort has no recurring personal meaning, or support is readily accepted without identity concern.
sections.title: Use safer conditions and accepted help as tests

sections.body_md: Evidence tied to one instrument cannot establish a universal subtype. This page cannot predict resilience, health, hardship, work capacity, or coping outcomes.
sections.title: Keep endurance observations non-predictive

sections.body_md:
Duration: 5

Context: Choose two difficult tasks with similar stakes but different disclosure safety, plus one period when strain eases.

Observable signal: Record effort, practical consequence, personal meaning, help available, refusal cost, disclosure, and change after conditions improve.

Page-specific signal: Compare the exact expression and help-seeking change when safety improves while task difficulty stays similar.

Alternative explanation: Compare caregiving, money, discrimination, migration, culture, role duty, and available support.

Reflection prompt: Identify whether necessity explains contained effort better than subtype and cite one disconfirming observation.

seo.description: Self-preservation Type Four is a traditional, evidence-limited hypothesis that identity-and-meaning attention may appear through contained expression, endurance, and personally significant effort under practical strain. Endurance cannot establish subtype because caregiving, unsafe settings, financial limits, and role duty can require the same restraint.
seo.title: Self-preservation Type Four: contained meaning under strain as a matched-comparison hypothesis
